title: DR1 lists JPG among the file formats a document can be in; the frontend's list omits JPG even though it accepts .jpg files.

finding.frontend: The second bullet reads "a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, PNG, XLS or XLSX" — seven formats, no JPG. A .jpg file is in fact accepted: it is in the allowed set and in the picker's accept attribute (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:10-11,24-26). It disappears from the hint because the hint is built by collapsing the allowed set on MIME type and JPG shares image/jpeg with JPEG, so only the first of the pair survives (:28-36). The same collapsed list is reused verbatim in the rejection message, so a user whose file is rejected for some other reason reads a list that does not include the extension they are holding.
finding.prototype: The second bullet reads "PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX" — eight formats, JPEG and JPG named separately (app/views/upload-documents.html:167).
finding.difference: List JPG alongside JPEG in the file-type hint and in the file-type rejection message. The fix is in how the hint is derived: build the label list from the allowed extensions rather than from their MIME types, so that formats sharing a MIME type are both named. The accepted set itself does not change.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding JPG named in the frontend's file-type hint or in its "The selected file must be a …" message.

relatedTo.why: both are bullets of the same requirements list
